proposedOverrides.summary: A cautious guide to late-medieval England and mapped possessions, with daily life, power, plague, print, and atlas border errors made explicit.

batchIdentityNotes: English territory is a generated atlas label, not a contemporary state name.
All three snapshots include many audited English and Welsh points, nearly all Ireland, and Gascony; the map omits sampled Calais, Tintagel, and Conwy.
The map greatly overstates uniform English authority in Ireland and preserves Gascony until 1492 although Bordeaux fell in 1453.
The 1279 and 1300 geometries are byte-identical after decoding; 1400 has tiny transform drift with unchanged sampled membership.
Claims are localized to named places and source types rather than projected over every polygon component.
The 1492 endpoint is an id switch to england-1492 under Henry VII, not the fall of England or disappearance of any population.
